decisions.title: Too busy to be tired
decisions.situation: Robin says it is time for a nap. You have been awake for ages and have only inspected half the room.

choices.label: Give your eyes a short test closure
Ask Robin to stay for a minute
Explain your position at full volume

result.title: Test extended
result.body: You wake up later. The uninspected half of the room is still there.

journal.text: I fell asleep while checking whether I needed a nap.

decisions.title: The two-headed jacket
decisions.situation: You manage to zip two jackets together. They are now one enormous jacket with four sleeves. This may be your greatest invention.

choices.label: Carefully separate the creature
Investigate whether a third one would fit
Leave your invention on the floor

result.title: Back to two jackets
result.body: You work out which zip goes where. Both jackets survive the experiment.

journal.text: I worked out how to separate two jackets I had zipped together.

decisions.title: Two is more than one
decisions.situation: Your biscuit breaks in half. There are now two biscuits, although something about the total feels suspicious.

choices.label: Fit the halves back together
Celebrate the extra biscuit
Count all the little crumbs

result.title: The original arrangement
result.body: The edges match. You test them twice before accepting that both pieces were one biscuit.

journal.text: I fitted two broken biscuit halves back together.

decisions.title: A very short biography
decisions.situation: Sophie passes you a homemade book called “People Who Smell Weird”. Your name is on page one. Every other page is blank.

choices.label: Give it a terrible review
Ask why they made it about you
Write their name on every remaining page

result.title: Needs more characters
result.body: You write “repetitive, poorly researched” on the cover. Sophie laughs, then admits they could not think of a second chapter.

journal.text: I reviewed Sophie’s insulting homemade book as a disappointed critic.

decisions.title: An unclaimed contribution
decisions.situation: A loud fart interrupts the lesson. Sophie Wilson (classmate) looks straight at you. Their face suggests a serious conflict of interest.

choices.label: Keep your face impressively neutral
Whisper that the chair needs repairing
Name your prime suspect at full volume

result.title: Lesson continues
result.body: Sophie Campbell (teacher) carries on. Sophie Wilson (classmate) eventually stops looking at you.

journal.text: I ignored a suspicious look after a loud noise in class.

decisions.title: Indoor architecture
decisions.situation: Rain cancels your afternoon plans. Two chairs and a blanket suggest a career in questionable structural engineering.

choices.label: Build an elaborate fort
Read by the window
Declare the whole day ruined

result.title: Approved for immediate occupancy
result.body: It collapses twice. The third version has a reading corner.

journal.text: I built a blanket fort that almost met building regulations.

decisions.title: The headteacher is three mice
decisions.situation: Sophie wants help with a class newsletter. The headline is “Headteacher Replaced by Three Mice”. Their evidence is a chewed worksheet.

choices.label: Investigate before printing it
Draw a wanted poster for the mice
Leave the rodent conspiracy to them

result.title: One human, several questions
result.body: The headteacher is visibly one person. Sophie reluctantly changes the headline to “Worksheet Damaged”. Your reporting improves; circulation probably will not.

journal.text: I helped Sophie check a ridiculous newsletter claim.

decisions.title: Glitter lockdown
decisions.situation: You spill a pot of glitter during a class project. Sophie finds some inside a closed book.

choices.label: Help clean every desk
Make a paper funnel for next time
Try blowing it away

result.title: Still sparkling
result.body: You clean until the bell. There is probably some glitter left in the building forever.

journal.text: I helped clean a classroom after spilling glitter everywhere.

decisions.title: Your name on the cover
decisions.situation: Sophie asks you to share a class project. Charlie has given you two months. That sounds like a problem for Future You.

choices.label: Promise to write your section
Ask to work separately
Admit you cannot commit

result.title: Future You has been notified
result.body: You agree on a section to write. The deadline is saved; agreeing has not completed any work.

journal.text: I agreed to write a section of a class project with Sophie.

decisions.title: The project is due
decisions.situation: Sophie is putting the class project together. Charlie wants your section today. The blank page has enjoyed two months of peace.

choices.label: Finish your section
Ask Charlie for help
Leave your section blank

result.title: Your name belongs on it
result.body: You finish your section and explain it to Sophie. Charlie records the work you actually did.

journal.text: I finished my section of the class project with Sophie.

decisions.title: Your stand-in has a meeting
decisions.situation: To dodge chores, you left a dummy in your dressing gown at your desk. Robin is now giving it a serious talk about responsibility. The dummy is handling it well.

choices.label: Step out and take over the discussion
Leave a second dummy to play Robin
Stay hidden and let the dummy handle it

result.title: A noticeable improvement in posture
result.body: Robin says the dummy already agreed to take the rubbish out. You do it while the dummy remains at the desk, apparently thinking about its future.

journal.text: I replaced a dummy during Robin’s lecture and did the chore it had agreed to.

decisions.title: A promise remembered
decisions.situation: Two years after that class project, Sophie Wilson brings it up. Back then, you finished your section.

choices.label: Remember doing your part
Tell Sophie it does not matter
Leave it in the past

result.title: An old project, an honest conversation
result.body: You acknowledge that you finished your section. Sophie hears you out.

journal.text: I talked honestly with Sophie about our old project, when I finished my section.

decisions.title: One star. Still hungry.
decisions.situation: Sophie drafts a fake restaurant review of the school canteen. It includes the phrase “structural pasta”.

choices.label: Turn it into useful feedback
Keep the joke between you
Read it aloud in class

result.title: Less funny, more useful
result.body: You keep the specific complaints and remove the insults. Charlie helps pass it on.

journal.text: I helped Sophie turn a canteen rant into useful feedback.

decisions.title: The cake has a message
decisions.situation: Sophie made a cake iced with an insult about Charlie. It was meant for a private joke. Charlie has just asked what is in the box.

choices.label: Eat the incriminating slice immediately
Tell Charlie what the cake says
Open the box and offer them a slice

result.title: The evidence was mostly icing
result.body: You stuff the message into your mouth. Charlie asks a second question, which you cannot answer. Sophie struggles not to laugh.

journal.text: I ate a slice of Sophie’s cake to hide its insulting message.

decisions.title: Before answering immediately
decisions.situation: A mildly irritating question arrives while you are already tired. You notice the sharp reply forming before the other person has finished speaking.

choices.label: Take a moment before answering
Say you need a short break
Deliver the sharp reply

result.title: A reply with less edge
result.body: The pause gives you time to separate the question from your tiredness. You answer the thing that was actually asked.

journal.text: I paused before answering sharply when I was tired.

decisions.title: The lost hand
decisions.situation: You pick up a glove from a bench. A rubber hand slides out of its sleeve. It has painted fingernails, a wristwatch and no obvious owner.

choices.label: Carry it to reception
Leave it upright on the bench
Ask around for anyone missing a hand

result.title: Please wave if this is yours
result.body: The receptionist holds the hand above the counter. A magician hurries over, thanks you and immediately removes its thumb. You stop watching.

journal.text: I returned a magician’s rubber hand to reception.

decisions.title: Nothing to worry about
decisions.situation: At a free repair demonstration, a wind-up toy starts smoking. The volunteer explains that it is supposed to do that. The label “DO NOT WIND” drops off its base.

choices.label: Ask what the label means
Step back and let them stop it
Ask whether smoke costs extra

result.title: A useful admission
result.body: The volunteer stops and explains the failed mechanism. You learn more from the mistake than from the planned demonstration.

journal.text: I asked about a warning label during a failed toy-repair demonstration.

decisions.title: Water with a personal brand
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, a presenter claims their water has been “emotionally filtered”. The jug beside it is labelled TAP. You are just thirsty.

choices.label: Drink the tap water
Ask which emotions the filter removes
Debate the emotional lives of liquids

result.title: No emotional processing required
result.body: It tastes like water. The presenter watches you finish a glass with the expression of someone witnessing sabotage.

journal.text: I chose tap water at a premium-water demonstration.

decisions.title: A minute without filling it
decisions.situation: You have a short wait with nothing to do. Before reaching for a distraction, you notice you have already checked the same screen three times.

choices.label: Look around for a minute
Let your attention rest
Check the same screen again

result.title: The world supplies a few details
result.body: You notice a small sign and an interesting pattern of light. The wait becomes a moment rather than a gap to erase.

journal.text: I spent a short wait noticing what was around me.

decisions.title: Your shoulders have a complaint
decisions.situation: After sitting in the same position for a while, you notice that your shoulders appear to have crept up towards your ears.

choices.label: Take a gentle movement break
Change your position and relax your shoulders
Stay exactly as you are

result.title: A different position helps
result.body: You loosen up at a comfortable pace and return to what you were doing. You had not noticed how stiff you were.

journal.text: I took a gentle movement break after sitting still.

decisions.title: A shortcut through the execution
decisions.situation: A museum shortcut in Vancouver takes you through a medieval punishment exhibit. A mechanical executioner swings a foam axe across the marked path. The long route has no executioner.

choices.label: Take the long route
Time the swing and walk through slowly
Sprint straight through the swinging axe

result.title: A head start
result.body: You turn back. A speaker announces, “The coward flees!” Three visitors turn to look. You continue with your head and your dignity approximately intact.

journal.text: I took the long route around a museum’s mechanical executioner.

choices.label: Write a clearer private reminder
Work backwards from the context
Assume it will make sense later

result.title: Future you gets better information
result.body: You replace the riddle with a useful explanation and keep it somewhere appropriate.

journal.text: I replaced an unhelpful private reminder with a clear one.

decisions.title: Honest feedback, preferably positive
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, you try a cracker that tastes strongly of cupboard. The demonstrator asks for a glowing testimonial while holding a camera.

choices.label: Suggest improving the flavour first
Praise how neatly it broke
Deliver a dramatic account of the cupboard

result.title: A review they can use
result.body: You mention the texture and the cupboard problem. The camera lowers. They admit this batch has been “challenging”.

journal.text: I gave specific criticism of a free food sample.

decisions.title: The sofa is judging you
decisions.situation: Autoplay follows your programme with a competitive fitness class. A man who appears to have been assembled entirely from elbows challenges you to beat your personal best.

choices.label: Switch to the beginner version and try it
Invent a chair-based version
Keep up with him at full speed

result.title: An achievable number of elbows
result.body: You complete the gentler routine. The instructor says anyone can do it, then folds himself into a shape you decline to investigate.

journal.text: I followed a beginner workout after a fitness video appeared on autoplay.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: persistent headaches and dizziness. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs CA$0.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

choices.label: Accept hospital assessment
Decline assessment

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: You said that part out loud
decisions.situation: You rehearse a devastating comeback while walking. A stranger turns around just as you announce, “That is why nobody trusts your ferret.”

choices.label: Explain that you were arguing in your head
Write the useful point down privately
Pretend to be on an important phone call

result.title: No actual ferret dispute
result.body: The stranger accepts the explanation and walks on a little faster. You retire the argument before it recruits anyone else.

journal.text: I stopped an imaginary argument after saying part of it aloud.

decisions.title: Any difficult questions?
decisions.situation: At a free talk, a speaker claims nobody has ever disproved their theory. The theory is that pigeons remember your face and discuss you at night.

choices.label: Ask how they interviewed the pigeons
Let another questioner take this one
Announce that the pigeons work for you

result.title: The method needs work
result.body: They admit they inferred the conversations. You learn the difference between a suspicious bird and actual evidence.

journal.text: I questioned the evidence behind a speaker’s theory about pigeons.

choices.label: Say your name clearly once more
Turn the correction into a light joke
Use the nickname for the afternoon

result.title: A manageable correction
result.body: The host repeats it correctly and moves on. The proposed nickname retires before its first appearance.

journal.text: I corrected my name instead of accepting an unwanted nickname.

decisions.title: Discreet volunteers wanted
decisions.situation: You post a request for cleanup volunteers in a community chat. Your phone attaches an old shopping list: bleach, bin bags and cable ties. Someone replies, “What exactly are we cleaning?”

choices.label: Explain that it is a garden cleanup
Delete the post without explaining
Add “No questions. Bring gloves.”

result.title: The photographs help
result.body: You attach a photo of weeds and broken plant pots. Two people volunteer. A third asks for a picture of you holding today’s newspaper. You decline that part.

journal.text: I explained a suspicious shopping list attached to my garden-cleanup request.

decisions.title: Wealth you cannot see
decisions.situation: A free gallery in Vancouver displays an empty plinth titled “My Invisible Yacht”. A visitor says only rich people can understand it. You can see the same amount of yacht as everyone else.

choices.label: Ask the guide what the work means
Admire its excellent fuel economy
Pretend to fall overboard

result.title: A surprisingly useful explanation
result.body: The guide says it is about status and imaginary ownership. The visitor looks relieved that somebody has supplied an answer.

journal.text: I asked about an invisible-yacht artwork in Vancouver.

decisions.title: In loving memory of the wrong man
decisions.situation: A public meeting in Vancouver unveils a proposed memorial bench. Its plaque honours a man who is alive, in the room, and asking whether this affects his parking permit.

choices.label: Suggest checking the plaque first
Hear the allegedly deceased man out
Leave before the eulogy

result.title: Death withdrawn from the proposal
result.body: You help redirect the discussion towards correcting the inscription. The man asks to keep “much loved” if possible.

journal.text: I suggested correcting a memorial plaque for a living man in Vancouver.

choices.label: Explain that you meant the soup
Leave the soup to its lawyers
Publish a detailed attack on their diagram

result.title: A narrow defence
result.body: You clarify that your review concerns lunch rather than civilisation. The diagram receives no further comment.

journal.text: I clarified a soup review after a stranger took it personally.

decisions.title: Inner peace is on hold

choices.label: Close your eyes and let them finish
Find peace on a walk outside
Offer to fix the printer problem

result.title: A guided loss of temper
result.body: You breathe slowly through an argument about toner. By the time they hang up, you are considerably calmer than the professional.

journal.text: I relaxed through my relaxation instructor’s furious printer call.

decisions.title: The song of extra garlic
decisions.situation: At a community singalong, the lyric projector fails. It starts displaying a takeaway receipt instead. The backing track continues. Everyone looks to you for the first line.

choices.label: Sing the receipt with feeling
Pass the microphone down the row
Demand that they restore the proper words

result.title: Hold the onions
result.body: You hit the high note on “extra garlic”. The room joins in for “delivery instructions”. The organiser finally switches off the projector during the sauce options.

journal.text: I led a singalong using a takeaway receipt as the lyrics.

choices.label: Write back about the sheet
List what you did achieve
Send your younger self a furious reply

result.title: The corners remain hostile
result.body: You report that the elastic corners remain a problem. You omit finances; you are not being interrogated by a child with a felt-tip pen.

journal.text: I answered an old note about being wealthy and folding fitted sheets.

choices.label: Tell them what your days actually involve
Say the birds are frightened of you
Describe every activity they failed to imagine

result.title: An overdue factual check
result.body: You give a short answer. They apologise for inventing your schedule before learning your name.

journal.text: I corrected a stranger’s assumption about my daily life.

Host exactly five minutes of nothing
Send an agenda for competitive relaxing

result.title: A successful cancellation

journal.text: I cancelled accidental invitations to my free hour.

choices.label: Admit you may be mixing memories
Stick to the part you remember clearly
Continue towards the dramatic ending

result.title: The audience understands
result.body: Someone else recognises the film. Your actual memory survives with a much smaller car chase.

journal.text: I corrected a memory that had borrowed a scene from a film.

decisions.title: The programme is now retro

choices.label: Enjoy noticing what has changed
Describe one detail you remember clearly
Object to the entire concept of retro

result.title: An accidental historical perspective
result.body: You spot details that once passed unnoticed. Familiarity gives you another way to watch it.

journal.text: I enjoyed seeing an old programme presented as a period piece.

choices.label: Ask what you are being thanked for
Return the microphone immediately
Thank everyone who made this possible

result.title: The right person is found
result.body: You were mistaken for the person who fixed a blocked toilet. Their arrival receives the applause they earned.

journal.text: I corrected a mistaken public thank-you before giving a speech.

decisions.title: A striking resemblance

Ask for a pencil and draw the artist
Cover the portrait and leave

journal.text: I asked a caricaturist to correct my portrait and received a thumb in a bow tie.

Work out what you used to enjoy
Watch the whole thing out of loyalty

journal.text: I stopped pretending to enjoy an old favourite programme.
